newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil plans powerful new telecom watchdog - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil plans powerful new telecom watchdog - report.

text.p: Brazil's future telecom policy will be regulated by an independent watchdog charged with granting concessions and setting rates, according to a draft of a telecommunications bill leaked to a local news agency.
Brazil's Broadcast news agency, which said it obtained the draft from unnamed market sources, published elements of the new law, expected to be sent to Congress this week.
The report could not be independently verified.
The report did not shed any light on how the government plans to break up and privatize federal telecom giant Telebras to hear about, analysts said.
Analysts said the draft provided some details, but did not contain any real surprises, although shares of Telebras shot up after the Broadcast report.
"There was no really big news," said Jacopo Valentino, a telecom analyst for German bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
According to the agency, the bill contains the following main points:
- Brazil's telecom policy will be set a new regulating agency named the Brazilian Telecommunications Agency (Agencia Brasileira de Telecomunicacoes - ABT).
- The ABT will be comprised of a Board of Directors, an Advisory Board as well as legal and watchdog entities.
- The ABT will establish the rules determining the concession of private and public telecommunication services.

- The ABT will ensure competition in the sector by preventing a concentration in the marketplace, establishing restrictions, limits and conditions for the granting of concessions to companies already providing telecom services.
- Telecom firms that invest at least two percent of gross operating revenue in research and development projects in Brazil will win tax and customs incentives.

- Telecom concessions will have a maximum term of 20 years, renewable once for up to the same period and only if the concessionaire expresses interest in the renewal at least 30 months prior to expiration.
- The ABT will set rates policy and may allow operators to set their own rates, under ABT supervision, after five years if it feels there is ample competition.
- The ABT can intervene in a concession if services are halted without good reason; for poor service; or for financial troubles stemming from mismanagement and threatening services.
- To maintain a concession, the concessionaire must meet certain requirements, including offering greater services, improving service quality, technological development and free competition.
